ShimuraCompactifications.title: Analytic toric geometry, Part II: arithmetic toroidal compactifications
ShimuraCompactifications.reason: The member already imports the common toric vocabulary. Make that boundary enforceable: the anchor owns its finite regular complex-fan constructions; the extension owns arithmetic-admissible fan systems, relative and integral torus embeddings, Shimura boundary quotients and their compactifications. Preserve the roadmap id and all nine stage ids. The unchanged Analytic toric geometry roadmap (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AnalyticToricGeometry) is the first prerequisite; the introduction must state exactly where its finite-complex scope stops.

ShimuraCompactifications:C0.keeps: Arithmetic-admissible cone collections on the common lattice/cone carriers, with arithmetic actions, finitely many cone orbits, local finiteness in the positivity domain, cusp support and compatibility; existence of common and sufficiently fine smooth/projective refinements, including cases not proved by the anchor; compatibility with parabolic inclusions and level changes; extension of affine toric charts to the required base rings, relative torus-torsor embeddings by descent, and the relative/arithmetic support-properness theorem under its separately verified finiteness and base hypotheses. Prove compatibility with the anchor on finite complex fans. Do not redefine its cones, finite fans, dual monoids or complex affine schemes.
ShimuraCompactifications:C0.reason: Finite-fan combinatorics and complex toric charts are imported from L0, and finite regular complex-fan properness from L5. Finiteness modulo an arithmetic group is not finiteness of the fan. L0 defines subdivisions; it does not supply the required existence of common, smooth or projective refinements.

ShimuraCompactifications:C1.reason: Keep the enrichment of V2 boundary components, mixed Shimura boundary data, positivity cones, pure quotients, torus/abelian torsors, cusp labels and stabilizers. Continue to import, rather than reconstruct, the existing linear-algebraic mixed Hodge structures and the common lattice/cone vocabulary.

ShimuraCompactifications:C2.keeps: Partial compactifications of C1 boundary torus torsors using C0 embeddings; their arithmetic transition, separation, quotient and gluing proofs; normality, properness and the open immersion; descent of the local boundary description at neat level for smooth fans; projectivity for projective admissible fans; the map to the existing minimal compactification and its boundary fibers; canonical-model descent in the stated datum class. Any nonregular-cone geometry required by the original normality/properness targets remains an extension obligation. Prove comparison on finite split complex charts instead of reconstructing those charts, their fan gluing or their local toric boundary theorem.
ShimuraCompactifications:C2.reason: The finite regular complex chart, gluing and boundary lemmas are exact upstream subproblems, not the full arithmetic construction. Neither arithmetic quotient separation nor canonical-model descent follows merely from finite-fan gluing. The original normal-crossings conclusion is not silently strengthened to global simple normal crossings after quotienting.

ShimuraCompactifications:C2.general.reason: Retain C2 plus ShimuraVarieties:V8.general as the general-data descent interface, with the same rational boundary components and stabilizers. Import the narrowed C2 construction and the named finite-chart suppliers, not a second gluing theory.

ShimuraCompactifications:C3.keeps: Descent and gluing of refinement maps on the arithmetic toroidal models, with identity/composition laws and agreement with L5 on finite regular complex toric charts; extensions of datum morphisms and Hecke translations for compatible fans; comparison of choices through C0 common refinements; structure-sheaf pushforward and normality theorems; separately stated higher-direct-image vanishing for the exact coefficient sheaves and hypotheses used by consumers.
ShimuraCompactifications:C3.reason: L5 owns ordinary finite regular toric maps and proper subdivision maps, including the star-subdivision test. It does not own arithmetic Hecke extensions, general refinement pushforward, or coefficient-specific higher-direct-image vanishing.

ShimuraCompactifications:C3.general.reason: Retain the general-data level/refinement/Hecke and boundary comparisons on C2.general. No all-prime integral assertion or new generic finite-fan construction is added.

ShimuraCompactifications:C4.keeps: Relative semi-abelian degeneration over the cusp bases: character groups and extensions of abelian schemes by tori, biextensions, polarized 1-motive degeneration data, relative algebraization/effectivity, formal universal charts, extension of endomorphisms and boundary level comparisons. Extend the existing common local Raynaud/abelian-uniformisation construction of R11.3, retaining its polarization, lattice and base hypotheses and proving specialization compatibility; do not construct that local theory a second time. The local theorem does not itself prove relative effectivity or the universal PEL degeneration. Import split tori over a commutative base and C0 relative toric geometry, and retain every dimension-one comparison with ModularCurvesPartII R13.1–R13.3, including du/u versus dq/q and ramified p-level cusp maps.
ShimuraCompactifications:C4.reason: AUDIT-10 flags the local Raynaud extension and polarized lattice-uniformisation subproblem in both stages. R11.3 explicitly owns it, also recorded by RS-25; C4 builds on that local case using the same carriers, and owns the additional relative cusp/1-motive/effectivity construction and its comparison, not a second local uniformisation. This does not extend any upstream anchor or identify semistable reduction with boundary effectivity.

ShimuraCompactifications:C5.reason: Retain good-prime integral PEL toroidal algebraic spaces, universal semi-abelian extensions, formal completions, properness, Hodge positivity, section finite generation, minimal projectivity, open quasi-projectivity and higher-p-level normalization bounds. Complex toric properness is only a compatibility input, never a proof of these integral conclusions.

ShimuraCompactifications:C6.reason: Retain the Hilbert ordinary-neighborhood models, cusp lattices and unit quotients, polarization quotient comparisons, Hasse ideals, modular comparison at the stated levels, and the coefficient-appropriate Koecher and boundary-ideal statements. Ramified Hilbert geometry continues to use H2, not an enlarged good-prime claim for C5.
